name: The Herzogspark Plane
verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Regensburg (Naturdenkmal Nr. 10, designated under the city's Naturdenkmal-SicherungsVO, consolidated version of 24 August 2007)

https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Regensburg-HerzogsparkPlatane-1-Asio.JPG (photographer's own dated description, 29 August 2022: '200-jährige Platane (Naturdenkmal) in dem als Naturdenkmal geschützten Herzogspark')
access: Free. Inside the Herzogspark, a public municipal park at the northwestern edge of the Altstadt, open daily during daylight hours.
transport: Regensburg Hauptbahnhof, then about a 15-20 minute walk, or bus to Prebrunn/Herzogspark stop, 5 minute walk.
verify_notes: One of Regensburg's individually protected Naturdenkmal trees (city ordinance no. 10, part of the consolidated Naturdenkmal-Sicherungsverordnung, most recent notice 24 August 2007). The Herzogspark itself dates to a 1804 private garden laid out for Georg Friedrich von Mueller on the site of the old Prebrunn bastion, passed to the Thurn und Taxis family in 1843, bought by the city in 1935 and reopened as a public park in 1950-1952 (source: de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzogspark). The 'roughly 200 years' age comes from a single photographer's on-site caption (Wikimedia Commons, 2022) rather than an official survey; treat as an estimate and flag. No source states the tree was part of the original 1804 planting; do not bridge the park's founding date to the tree's age, they are two separate facts. Coordinates are the photo's own GPS tag, which places it inside the park boundary. The plane stands near the Prebrunnturm, the medieval gate tower that anchors the park, which is a nice visual pairing for the story (a 200-year-old tree beside a 700-year-old tower).

name: The Chestnuts of Am Gries
age_estimate: not documented; mature specimens, one in visible decline as of 2022
verified_sources: https://www.regensburg.de/stadtrecht/233932/verordnung-zur-sicherung-von-naturdenkmalen-im-stadtgebiet-von-regensburg-nd-sicherungsvo-in-der-fassung-der-bekanntmachung-vom-24-august-2007.html (city ordinance, 'Kastanien Am Gries', Naturdenkmal Nr. 52, designated 28 March 1996)

Bavaria LfU state Naturdenkmal register, entry ND-03369 'Naturdenkmal Kastanien am Gries, St. Regensburg' (independent state-level designation, coordinates ~250m from the photographed trees, same street)
access: Free. Street trees on Am Gries in Stadtamhof, visible and reachable from the public street.
transport: Across the Steinerne Brücke (Stone Bridge) from the Altstadt, then about a 5 minute walk along Am Gries.
verify_notes: IMPORTANT vitality flag: the Commons photo (taken 29 August 2022) is explicitly captioned 'mit der absterbenden Kastanie im Vordergrund' (with the dying chestnut in the foreground), meaning at least one of the ensemble's chestnut trees was visibly declining four years ago. This is a small group (the city ordinance and the Wikipedia list both describe it as a cluster, 'Kastanien Am Gries', not a single trunk), so the entry can still ship honestly as an ensemble as long as the story does not claim all trees are thriving; a future run or reader should re-check current condition. Designated by the city in 1996 and separately by the Bavarian state Naturdenkmal register (ND-03369), which counts as two independent official sources for existence, species and protected status, though neither register gives an age. The state register's own coordinate (49.02376, 12.09964) sits about 250m west of the photographer's GPS-tagged position; the photo coordinate is used here as the more precise, tree-level fix, and the discrepancy is ordinary register-geocoding slack, not a conflicting fact. A second, similarly-named Naturdenkmal chestnut group stands two doors down at Am Gries 30 ('Rosskastanien Zum Goldenen Löwen', see rgb_003); the two are a five-minute walk apart on the same street in Stadtamhof and pair naturally in a walk.

name: The Chestnuts of the Golden Lion
verified_sources: https://www.regensburg.de/stadtrecht/233959/ (city ordinance, 'Rosskastanien Zum Goldenen Loewen in Stadtamhof', Naturdenkmal Nr. 53, designated 11 June 1997)
access: Free. Street trees at Am Gries 30 in Stadtamhof, visible and reachable from the public street; named for the former Zum Goldenen Loewen inn on the same plot.
transport: Across the Steinerne Bruecke (Stone Bridge) from the Altstadt, then about a 5 minute walk along Am Gries.
verify_notes: Named for the historic Zum Goldenen Loewen inn that once stood on this Stadtamhof plot; the register description (per de.wikipedia.org's Naturdenkmaeler list) notes the designation covers '1 Rosskastanie und Torso' (one horse chestnut plus a torso/stump of a second), so this is a smaller, possibly partly-lost group rather than a grand avenue; a future pass or reader should confirm current state. Only one independent official source (the 1997 city ordinance) plus the dated Commons photo; no Bavaria state register match found within 3km other than the Am Gries 18 entry (rgb_002), which is a separate designation. No age recorded anywhere; leave age_estimate empty rather than guess and let the page ask the reader. Pairs with rgb_002 (five minutes' walk on the same street) for a short Stadtamhof leg of a Regensburg walk.

name: The Plane of the Old Corn Market

location.address: Alter Kornmarkt, Regensburg (south side, near the Alte Kapelle bell tower)
location.neighbourhood: Altstadt (old town, UNESCO World Heritage site)

verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Regensburg (Naturdenkmal Nr. 34, "Platane", "Am Alten Kornmarkt", designated under the city Naturdenkmal-SicherungsVO)
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Naturdenkmal_Platane_am_Alten_Kornmarkt_(Regensburg).jpg (dated photograph, taken 11 August 2024, confirming the tree currently stands)
access: Free. Standing on or beside the Alter Kornmarkt, a public square in the historic centre used for a weekly Saturday vegetable market; open at all times.
transport: In the Altstadt, about a 10 minute walk from Regensburg Hauptbahnhof, next to the Roman-era Roemerturm and Herzogshof.
verify_notes: One of Regensburg's individually protected Naturdenkmal trees, standing on the Alter Kornmarkt, a nearly-square Roman-era market place (ca. 175 AD origins per de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alter_Kornmarkt) at the heart of the UNESCO-listed old town, ringed by the Herzogshof, the Roemerturm and the Karmelitenkloster. The Wikipedia article on the square itself describes a row of trees on the south side that partly hides the freestanding bell tower of the Alte Kapelle ('hinter einer Baumreihe verborgen'), which is the likely position of this plane, but no source gives an exact address or GPS fix for the tree itself, so the pin is set to the square's own centre and marked approximate rather than guessed precise. No age is recorded anywhere; leave the field empty and let the page ask a reader with a tape measure. The 2024 photograph confirms the tree is alive and standing as of last year.

name: The Plane at Singrün Corner

location.address: Corner of Prebrunnstrasse and Am Singruen, Regensburg

verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Regensburg (Naturdenkmal Nr. 43, "Platane am Singruen", "Ecke Prebrunnstrasse - Am Singruen", city Naturdenkmal-SicherungsVO)
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:ND_Platane_am_Singr%C3%BCn_(Regensburg).jpg (dated photograph, taken 15 September 2024, confirming the tree currently stands)
access: Free. Standing at a public street corner in the Prebrunn district, visible and reachable at any time.
transport: About a 10-15 minute walk from Regensburg Hauptbahnhof; a 5 minute walk from the Herzogspark (rgb_001), on the same side of the old town.
verify_notes: One of Regensburg's individually protected Naturdenkmal street trees, at the corner of Prebrunnstrasse and Am Singruen, a short walk from the Herzogspark plane (rgb_001), which makes a natural short extension to that stop on a walk. No GPS tag on the source photograph and no street-number address in the register description, only the street corner, so the pin uses the corner's geocoded position and is marked approximate rather than a guessed exact trunk position. No age or girth recorded anywhere. The September 2024 photograph confirms the tree is alive and standing as of last year, which is the strongest recency evidence in this batch.
